utterances.text: My answer was "yes," but here it says "no interpretation."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I would like to move on discussing the methodology in your report as I said at the beginning of my re-examination, and I would like you to turn to paragraph 595 in your report. Do you have this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you say in paragraph 595 is that for each of the events you were asked to address, you attempted, as best as possible, to apply a certain methodology. Can you further describe your methodology where it's included at paragraph 595 and say why you decided to adopt such a methodology. Excuse me, general, there is no interpretation, at least on my screen. Can you start again your response to my question which was: Can you further describe your methodology as it is included in paragraph 595 of your report and say or explain why you decided to adopt such a methodology.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, there were a certain number of events, five, six or seven events. Although these events are different, in terms of their essence were different. However, at the same time, in spite of these differences, all of these events were related to each other and there were certain similarities between these events. And the key issue when selecting my methodology was to determine how to deal with these events, which methodology to apply to them. And I wanted to apply one methodology when dealing with all the events. So as to cover all of the essential issues that related to the events, to deal with all the similarities between the events. This is why the methodology I used was the methodology described in paragraph 595, or rather, I applied these five principles: Number 1; description of the event; number 2, the relationship between each of the events and the corps commander or brigade commander; number 3, I stated what one could expect from a corps commander and from a brigade commander in relation to such an event; under number 4, I described the steps actually taken by commanders or, rather, commands in relation to the event, and depending on the event concerned; and finally, under number five, I presented my conclusion, that was naturally the result of the previous principles described. That would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I would like to turn to a paragraph in your report, which is paragraph 663. Actually, I would like to refer to paragraph 663 until 668. And my question is: Is there any information in the description of this event which does not come from the material that was given to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't include anything in this report if it was impossible to find confirmation in the documents that I have behind me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From 679 until 684 and the title is: "Actions taken in relation to the events in the Lasva Valley in January of 1993." And my question is the same, is there any information included in these paragraphs that does not come from the material which was made available to you to prepare your report?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when you say at paragraph 679 that - and I quote from the report - "It can be seen that General Hadzihasanovic issued numerous orders to ensure that subordinate commanders would inform all members of their units that no criminal activity would be tolerated and that measures would be taken if violations were committed," and then you go on to describe a number of actions. Did you actually see in writing, in the documents that were at your disposal, all of the actions that are described in these paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I read these documents with my very own eyes, and there is a significant number of such documents contained in these binders here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now if we look, General, at paragraph 688. Now I ask you this because my colleague from the Prosecution opted not to challenge your conclusions and that was his right, but looking at it from a methodology point of view, I look at the conclusion you reach at paragraph 688. And I ask you whether this conclusion is derived only from the material which was put at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly it was derived from the material placed at my disposal and to a minor extent I made assessments on the basis of my own experience. And I also relied on all of the documents I was provided with when making such assessments, when combining the documents that I had at my disposal and my experience. When viewing the situation from my own perspective, the perspective as a commander of the 1st Corps and when I regarded the situation from the perspective of the 3rd Corps commander, I made the comment that I made in paragraph 688.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question, General, is if I would go through Part IV of your report and take each of the events addressed in the report one by one and I would ask you the same questions, that is: Are your conclusions -- based on the material that you were given, as well as on your experience, would your answers be the same as you just provided for the events which allegedly took place in Dusina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question, General, is follows. The Prosecution has decided to -- or has attempted to challenge the drafting of your report -- of course they did not challenge any of your conclusions but that's a different matter -- but they attempted to challenge the drafting of your report and the validity of your report. We're not sure if they are saying that your report was bias, or if your report was -- the methodology was wrong. We're not sure exactly what the challenge is. But it is implicit that they are challenging your report. My last question is: What last information would you like to provide to the Trial Chamber with respect to the preparation of this report and how much weight we can give to your conclusions.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to the weight I would give to my report or rather to my conclusions, if one engaged someone else, an expert, had someone draft else drafted this report many of the commanders of the ABiH corps, in the course of the war and the Generals, members of the General staff of the ABiH, any of the politicians with knowledge of military matters because most of these are covered in the report concerning military matters, and naturally anyone from the ABiH and any of the politicians who was a member of the government or the Republic of Bosnia-Hercegovina, any of these people would have provided a very similar report if not an identical report in relation to many of the issues. And why do I say that? Because this certainly depicts the reality such as it was to a very large extent. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. That is what the situation was like, and generally speaking it was not different. There are certain nuances that could be introduced with regard to certain issues, but that's a different matter. What I have claimed is certainly the case and in a way that would be my response to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I must add one final question, General. When you agreed to take on this challenge as you described, and when you sat in this chair last Monday the 21st of March, was your aim to defend a friend, to protect the reputation of your country, to protect the reputation of your army, or to be an objective expert witness?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to the first part of your question, the objective of my report, the objective of my work, the final objective had a far wider scope than the objective of the Defence for General Hadzihasanovic and the Defence for Brigadier Kubura. The objective would be just to portray the reality of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina and, in particular, in Central Bosnia in the course of 1993. By viewing the situation from the perspective of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a state whose independence is internationally recognised, naturally the focus was also on the 3rd Corps and on the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. But as to the second part of your question, my objective was as follows: Because I'm deeply persuaded of the fact that in Bosnia-Herzegovina it's not necessary to say anything but the truth. The truth is the best guarantee for the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina for its continuity as a national entity, but especially from the perspective of the ABiH regardless of certain events, not only within the 3rd Corps, but in the entire ABiH the truth and only the truth is in fact the best guarantee for our future. And by following the truth, the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a state will be best preserved. And this is the principle that guided me and that would be my response -- that would be my response to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, maybe you did not understand my question. My question was simply what your objective was in drafting your report and in testifying before the Trial Chamber. Was it to be an objective expert witness? Or something else?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well I think that I understood your question and I have answered your question. My objective was to be as objective as possible, to appear here as an expert witness, to follow the truth and to be as objective as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this concludes my re-examination of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will now have our break and we will resume at five to one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now on to the Defence team of General Kubura.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, there is just one matter we wish to clarify in re-examination. Further cross-examination by Mr. Dixon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you may recall yesterday that Mr. Mundis put a hypothetical situation to you regarding Mr. Koricic, the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade and his leaving the brigade. I'm not going to go into whether that hypothetical is correct or not, that's a matter that was dealt with already in your examination-in-chief. All I want to look at, it's one clarification in respect of the effect of a commander leaving. You said in your examination-in-chief that article 78 of the decree law on service in ABiH, that's the decree of 1 August 1992, is the decree that governs that situation. I'm going to ask with the assistance of the usher if you could have a look at that article again. It's P243, and it's at page 42 of the B/C/S, page 17 of the English. If you could, General, please read article 78 again and then I wish to ask you one question about it. Can you firstly confirm that that is the provision that was in force in 1993.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, in response to a question asked by Mr. Mundis, that in the former rules of service in the JNA, that there was a provision which stated that for the first two months when a commander left, there was no requirement to have a written assignment and you cited the former rules of service in the JNA as your basis for making that statement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking again at Article 78, could you please clarify for the Trial Chamber - and as this may be an issue of some importance - that that two-month rule is not included in the provisions of Article 78. If you could answer for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that, according to the rules of service in the JNA as opposed to this book of rules and it's Article 78, that these are different and that the two month period that is mentioned in the JNA is not mentioned in this article here. However, according to my very deep belief, the rules of service of the JNA provided more clarification or intended to provide for more clarification and that is why one of the provisions provided for this two-month period as the deadline or the cut-off date when an order should have been issued by a superior officer deputising any officer to stand in for his commander or temporarily occupying a new position, which was probably done in view of the fact that this position might have to be applied during the wartime and that the order deputising a person cannot always be issued immediately, that sometimes it may take a few days and, in some other situations due to various circumstances, such an order may take up to two months. The two month period, however, is the longest period for any of the situations that any military may find themselves in, and this deadline was given for a written document to be issued to that effect. In Article 78 of this document, this hasn't been provided for. I believe that this was considered to be redundant and that's why it is not mentioned in this article here, for a very simple basic reason. It says in the article that the deputising position may last no longer than six months and, by decision of the second level superior, up to one year. There is absolutely not possible for the Chief of Staff standing in for the commander of the brigade for over a year without a written document, without a written order to that effect being issued. It goes against any of the doctrines, principles, and rules of any of the military. However, there is the two-month period which is provided for to cover for any objective circumstances and it is after the two-month period that the order has to be issued. This Article 78 implies precisely that, irrespective of the fact that it is not expressly spelled-out. This short period of time is the time during which deputising may be exercised without a written document. However, in the shortest possible time when the conditions for that in place, every deputising function has to be covered by a written document. I have tried to be as clear as possible in providing you with my answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Can I just pick up on one point that you made at the end, which is that you said in the shortest possible time, a written document must be forthcoming. Why is that the case?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this is requested by all the regulations. The military is the most specific body of any one society. In the military, the command and control function is exercised through orders, but orders can be both oral and verbal. However, it is provided for any verbal order to be covered by a written order issued in the shortest possible time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. One final question. You mentioned the formal rules of service in the JNA. Yesterday you were shown the rules of service in the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They are also part of P243 that you have there. Were those rules of service adopted at the same time as this decree law that we are referring to, where Article 78 is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure, but I don't think so. However, I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the rules of service that you were shown yesterday, were those the ones that were in force in Bosnia in 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they were in force already in that year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would that then mean that the rules of service in the JNA, which was the former army, were no longer applicable?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It goes without saying that once these rules were created and adopted, then the JNA rules stopped being valid or stopped being enforced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, General. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have about 20 or so questions to put to you. I don't think that the time that we have at our disposal will allow us to ask and answer all of the questions. Before I put my questions to you, I would like to reassure you immediately that the questions that I'm going to put to you will not intend to challenge the contents of your report, but rather to clarify certain aspects of your report and the paragraphs that you mention in your report. I am also going to ask you certain direct questions relative to certain parts of your report. My objective is to clarify the contents of your report and not to contest your report. The Prosecution has to appreciate our interest in finding the truth. My questions will serve just to clarify certain points. Questioned by the Court: And I am going to ask you immediately to go -- go to paragraph 4707 in your report, speaking of the questions that the Defence for General Kubura has asked you about, we would like to be clear on the issue of nominations. This paragraph, if I understand it well, it arises from this paragraph that on the 12 March 1993 Brigadier Kubura, which you have indicated, was appointed a Chief of Staff and at the same time he was the deputy commander, so he had two positions. He held two positions, he was the Chief of Staff and the deputy commander. And this happened on the 12th of March. Can you confirm that? Can you confirm that General Kubura, on the 12th of March 1993, held two positions?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. Who was the commander of the 7th brigade in that case?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Koricic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Where was Koricic? Amongst the documents that you studied, did you find the proof of Koricic's presence? Did he sign any orders? If he didn't, where was he, was he ill? Was he on holiday? Did he have any other temporary assignment? What can you tell us about the situation of Mr. Koricic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything particular with regard to Koricic. I was not in possession of any documents. Either they didn't exist or I wasn't given these documents that could tell me where Koricic was, what he did, what his status was. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. However, you've just said that he wasn't in the brigade, and asked me whether he was in the brigade, indeed. Yesterday I provided an answer to a similar question and I said that it doesn't really matter whether the brigade commander is in the brigade or outside of the brigade. In legal terms, in my view, and in military terms, it doesn't mean a thing. The brigade commander can be outside of the brigade. He can go to Tuzla, to Bihac, without his status of the brigade commander being changed. He remains the brigade commander no matter where he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If somebody is not present in a unit and you've just told us that, that he could be elsewhere, but he could also be ill or he could have been injured, maybe he could have undergone surgery, he could be abroad, there could be a different number of situations or scenarios possible. As an expert, did you ask yourself where Koricic was? Or you just started from the idea that he was there because you didn't see any document proving that he was either ill, or injured, or that he was on some mission? What made you say what you have just told us? What were the problems involved in that he was still the brigade commander and he was responsible for the brigade and he wasn't there? You yourself were the commander of the 1st Corps. Did you find yourself in the situation when the brigade commander wasn't there, but for you, he still held the position. Could you please clarify that. We are trying to understand, how is it possible for somebody who is not present to still be present in military sense?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right in the first part of your question when you asked me about Koricic's status. What was Koricic's status and what was his situation. You're absolutely right to ask me that. And you also asked me whether he was in a position to perform his duties as the brigade commander or not depending on the situation because if he was ill or if he had been killed or captured, objectively it would have been very hard for him to -- to perform his duties. However, for me to be able to assist in the proper sense, I would have to know the status that he was in at the time. And this status was supposed to be regulated by his superior officer. I did not come by any documents that would lead me to conclude what his status was, whether he fled to a third country, whether he was sent to a third country, maybe he wasn't in a third country at all. I really don't know. I can only assume -- maybe he was in Bosnia and Herzegovina for all I know. There are no documents proving one or the other. Wherever he was, he remained commander until he was dissolved from his duties. I started from the assumption that he was alive and well and that he performed the duties of the commander wherever he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So for you he was still the brigade commander until the 6th of August, at least?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would be more or less the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please look at the last sentence of this paragraph, which starts in English with the word "before." Look at it in your language, please. You say in here: Before that date, the 6th of August, 1993, he had sat as an acting commander of the brigade. What did you want to say with this sentence, in military terms, in a military sense? I'm not asking you to draw any conclusions, especially legal questions. In military terms, what did this mean for you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means as follows. Yesterday I also answered a very specific question to this effect. The situation, when Koricic -- and we only assume left for God knows what reasons from the brigade -- and let's say that he was no longer in command of the brigade, although I can start from another assumption and that is that he was in command, but we don't know that. But let's say that he was not in command of the brigade. The first in the chain of command below him was Brigadier Kubura. He already held two positions that we already discussed. He did not have any other solution but to continue working and leading the brigade in the way he could and the way he best knew how to. If he had said that he would no longer continue leading the brigade, it would have been dangerous for him. And this would have assumed more responsibility for him, because he failed to obey order and this is very dangerous in a state of war. For him to take this responsibility without being covered with an official piece of paper is also dangerous. He did ask for an order to be issued to cover his new duty, but this never came through as far as I know. In those simple terms, because of the situation on the ground, he just continued performing his duties, although it is questionable whether at that moment, given the fact that he was a very young man, at the moment whether he was mature enough, whether he had the qualities to be appointed either the commander or the acting commander of the brigade. Yesterday I said, what if his superiors had that in mind and that's why they hesitated to appoint him officially, as either the acting commander or the brigade commander. Maybe they had reservations about his qualities. However, the time when went by and the brigade as a living organism existed and this is how things went. I assume that this is how things went until the moment the decision was issued on appointing him first the acting commander and then the commander of the brigade and this was done by the supreme command and the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Hercegovina. And now when you look at the ambiguous status of Koricic as the brigade commander and where he was and whether he had the true authorities of the brigade wherever he was, this is all questionable. And as for Amir Kubura, irrespective of his situation and his qualities, he had been appointed on the 12th of March to the position of the Chief of Staff and this mind you is also very high position. And he held two positions at the same time. And because of the circumstances, he had to continue leading the brigade as best as he could. I am only trying to explain this, to clarify this particular situation and I don't know whether I've succeeded, or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Koricic was absent in the 1st Corps when the brigade commander was absent, did he have to ask for authorization to be absent? Did he have to inform the corps commander of his absence? Or was this done without any --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The commander cannot leave his position without his superior being aware of the fact. This is very dangerous in wartime, it is unacceptable. It is not in accordance with the regulations. That is certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean that in time military hierarchy above the commander of the 7th brigade felt that Koricic was present, occupied his post. If authorization had not been requested to be absent, does this mean that the Main Staff of the 3rd Corps command thought that Koricic could be reached around the clock?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is something that confuses me too. Because I cannot establish what the truth was. It's impossible for a superior not to be aware that Koricic was absent for such a long period of time. It's very difficult, even impossible. But on the other hand, if he did leave, whether someone authorised him to do so or not -- or if someone authorised to leave, this should have been regulated and certain documents and the status of Brigadier Kubura should have been regulated. This is a key issue. This is the key issue in the puzzle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly, you have had a look at all the documents and you didn't find a single document that defined Koricic's status, no documents that said that he was away on mission, ill, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see a single document of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would prefer to give the floor to the Defence and the Prosecution, if they want to ask any questions that relate to this issue so that we can avoid re-addressing the issue tomorrow. In this way we'll be able to maintain a certain pace. Mr. Mundis, are there any questions you would like to ask the witness with regard to this particular subject? Further cross-examination by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions, Mr. President, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to us in Koricic and his whereabouts, did anyone from either of the Defence teams inform you that Mr. Koricic testified in the Koricic case on the tenth of June of 1999?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Mr. Dixon. You're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I do want to object to this line of questioning, because my learned friend is going to refer to testimony in another case which is not evidence in this case. Mr. Koricic did testify in another trial and he did provide testimony regarding his situation, but the Prosecution never, ever sought to introduce that evidence in this trial and on that basis, although my friend does have a foundation to put the question, that isn't in evidence and I, therefore, would submit it would be unfair to now ask those questions and the answers then to become evidence in this trial. So I would object to this line of questioning. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You may ask the question whether he is aware of the fact that Koricic testified, but please don't mention the content of his testimony that is of no relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I assure you, Mr. President was not my intention to put any questions to the witness concerning the contents of Mr. Koricic's testimony, but simply whether the witness was aware of the fact. And I misspoke; it was actually in the Blaskic trial on the tenth of June 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir did anyone inform you that Mr. Koricic testified about these matters that we've been discussing here today in the Blaskic case on the 10th of June, 1999? Did anyone ever tell you that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he testified, but I don't know in which case. I don't know when and I don't know anything about the contents of his testimony and I don't know who told me about this either, but I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What steps, sir, if any, did you take in terms of following up on this information to answer these questions that you had concerning the whereabouts of Mr. Koricic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something I only gave thought to, but I didn't take any steps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, what steps, if any, did you take with respect to asking the Defence team for Mr. Kubura to provide you with information concerning the whereabouts of Mr. Koricic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the documents that I was provided with. Those are the only steps that I took. I didn't come across anything about this subject in the material that I came across. So the only steps I took were examining the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, sir, from a professional point of view, find it curious that there was no documentation concerning Mr. Koricic and his whereabouts during this time period?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well a minute ago that is what I said, in response to a question from the Presiding Judge. I said that one might think about what you just suggested, but I don't want to make any sort of projections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you find, sir, that the fact that your report, or in your report you were unable to draw any specific conclusions on this point -- is a gap in your report?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so because I had access to certain documents. I drafted my report on the basis of those documents. Your question is appropriate to a certain extent, but that is not the only question one could put. Many such questions could be phrased in relation to the voluminous content of this report, but I couldn't find certain documents, there were to such documents, I had no access to them. Whether something was behind this, I don't know. But given what I had access to, I clarified this situation, in terms of the facts that we had access to at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't take any steps in order to obtain the information with respect to the whereabouts of Mr. Koricic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what other steps I could have taken. If this Tribunal hasn't been able to obtain any other information -- information, I don't see how an expert witness could have obtained such information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to object to the question that the Prosecution just put to the witness. The questions that the Chamber put concerned military issues and the status of the commander who was present or absent. My colleague is taking opportunity of this situation to undermine the credibility of the witness, though he complained about the fact that the witness examined material outside of the documents he was provided with. The witness has expressed appear opinion on the basis of the documents. If my colleague wanted to say would things have been different if, this is a hypothetical question, then he can still put to the witness as a military expert. But there is no reason to ask him why he didn't go any further. He was provided with the documents. He did his work. My colleague could ask if Mr. Koricic had left such-and-such a date what would the conclusion have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, the Defence is saying that the expert did his work on the basis of his documents that he was provided with. Defence counsel can imagine a hypothesis that perhaps he could have acted otherwise. But that was not the case, he worked on the base he haves the volume news documents that are behind him. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Witness, you testified yesterday and again today in response to a question from my learned colleague, Mr. Bourgon, that you consulted with other former colleagues to verify information that you had. Did you consult with any former colleagues to verify the absence of confirmation concerning the whereabouts of Mr. Koricic in this time period?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This is the same type of question, and the objective of the question is identical. This has been covered at length. If my colleague wants to ask what the effect of the absence of an officer or presence of an absence is [as interpreted], that is permissible, but I don't think the questions can be put to obtain additional information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, please move on, because the expert has said that his work was based on the documents alone. He thought it was necessary to see other individuals from time to time, but if he had seen someone in relation to Koricic, I think that he would have mentioned the fact immediately. So please continue, because we only have a few more minutes and I know that Mr. Dixon has some questions to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No further questions on this issue, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Does Defence counsel for Mr. Hadzihasanovic have any questions or would you like to give the floor to Mr. Dixon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Dixon. Further cross-examination by Mr. Dixon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. There is only one matter which I wish to ask the General about. And that is whether, General, you had access, when you were preparing your report, to all the evidence presented by the Prosecution during the presentation of its case? In other words, all Prosecution documents, and all Prosecution witnesses that the Prosecution sought to rely upon. Did you have access to all of that material when you reviewed and prepared your report?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you prepared your conclusions, did you review all of that material and draw and base your conclusions upon the material that was given to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions on this subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have another 19 questions that will be dealt with tomorrow, but rest assured we'll be brief. General, tomorrow we will conclude with your testimony and it won't be necessary to continue with your examination on Friday. We will commence the hearing at 9.00 tomorrow but I have been asked to inform you of the following. Next week there won't be any hearings, because there are no witnesses who have been scheduled for that week. The hearings will recommence with Mr. Kubura's witnesses. They will commence again on the 11th of April, on Monday, next week. As I have said, there will be no hearings, and theoretically we should be in a position to conclude with the testimony of the expert witness tomorrow. Which means that on Friday there will be no hearing. I invite you all to appear for the hearing that will commence tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: be reconvened on, Thursday the 31st day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
